clue.text: Parents tour new American republic

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the parents' letters circle the next pieces

parts.note: PA and MA are both words for parents

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad take a newly arrived American on a trip around a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour' is the container signal: the parents go round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a Central American country governed as a republic.

clue.text: Start to bet when Bella's playing a game

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from bet

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the name is played about with, its letters rearranged

parts.note: a girl's name used as raw letters

explanation.surface: Someone places a first wager while Bella is busy at some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns BELLA into EBALL; the 's of Bella's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is a bat-and-ball sport, so it is a game.

clue.text: Figure hugging child's toy?

definitions.meaning: clothing that clings to the body's shape is ...
a coiled-spring toy that walks down stairs

explanation.surface: A tight dress or a toy that clasps a figure, as if a child were cuddling a doll.
explanation.definitionFit: Slinky describes close-fitting clothes and is also the brand of a coiled spring plaything.

clue.text: Very short alien green man's turned away

indicators.note: cutting the word alien very short leaves only its first letter

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
Ed is a man's name; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A tiny green Martian has swivelled round and looked elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the colour green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to turn something aside, so averted means turned away in the past tense.

clue.text: Monstrous woman who could be petrifying

definitions.text: Monstrous woman who could be petrifying

parts.words: Monstrous woman who could be petrifying
parts.note: petrifying is both terrifying and literally turning to stone, as the snake-haired Gorgon did to those who looked at her

explanation.surface: A frightening woman who might scare people stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Gorgon with snakes for hair turned onlookers to stone, literally petrifying them.

clue.text: Soft after exercise? Get fit, losing a stone

indicators.note: after says the soft piece follows the exercise piece

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
B marks a soft pencil lead

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word before

parts.note: fit can mean able, as in fit for the job

explanation.surface: A dieter after a workout hopes to shed fourteen pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing a' takes the A out of ABLE, leaving BLE. 'stone' looks like the weight being shed (a British stone is 14 lb) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small rounded rock, worn smooth by water.

clue.text: Battle over a party with Corbyn's lead — it's very hot!

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party

indicators.note: a word's lead is its first letter, here from Corbyn

parts.note: lava is molten rock, extremely hot

explanation.surface: A political party rallies behind Jeremy Corbyn in a heated fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns A LAB into BALA. Jeremy Corbyn led the UK Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Balaclava was an 1854 Crimean War engagement, famous for the Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: Asteroid at the heart of space research

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the phrase, across the boundary of its two words

explanation.surface: A rock in orbit that is central to astronomical study.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres was the first asteroid discovered, the largest body in the asteroid belt, now classed a dwarf planet.

clue.text: Show time raiding the larder

indicators.note: a raider breaks into a place, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pantry is a larder, a food store
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A display of time spent pilfering from the food cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate ceremonial display, a show of splendour.

clue.text: Manchester United manager once upset substitute with …

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense upset means turned over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: by can mean with, as in 'by hand'

explanation.surface: A football boss annoyed his replacement player.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Matt Busby managed Manchester United from 1945 to 1969.

clue.text: Theurgies regularly conjure up giant

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: Magic rituals routinely summon up a colossus.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge and giant are adjectives meaning enormous.

clue.text: … celebration and kiss beside unknown number of stars

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
in algebra Y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A party with kissing under the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system containing billions of stars.

clue.text: Trains Tom to wear suede pants

indicators.note: wearing something means being inside it, so one piece goes into the other
pants as slang for rubbish signals the word is messed up

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Tom is being taught to put on suede trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, an anagram signal giving EDUES; 'to wear' means to have the cat inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach them, so trains matches educates.

clue.text: 1st but not 2nd or 3rd of March …

indicators.note: the second and third letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: to troop is to march, as soldiers do

explanation.surface: The first day of March, not the second or third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but it is the verb, giving TROOP; dropping its 2nd and 3rd letters, R and O, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming top means finishing first, in the leading position.

clue.text: … a scorcher of a day!

definitions.meaning: the star in the sky that scorches the earth

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: what a hot day in March!
explanation.definitionFit: The star that burns overhead scorches, and the short form names the first weekday.

clue.text: Penny: "I will fight this case"

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Penny vows to contest a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillbox is a small container for tablets, a kind of case.

clue.text: Uranium discovered in lead bar

indicators.note: something found inside another thing sits within it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A radioactive element turns up within a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub is a drinking establishment, also called a bar.

clue.text: Fifty-fifty to catch Frisbee when laughing out loud

indicators.note: catching something holds it inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, given twice
a frisbee is a round disc, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An even chance of grabbing a flying disc while giggling.
explanation.definitionFit: LOL is the texting abbreviation for laughing out loud.

clue.text: Fine king stands on a lady's fingers

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the later ones

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A splendid king treads on a woman's fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's fingers is another name for the green pod vegetable used in gumbo.

clue.text: Father receives end of joke over 40 winks with a straight face

indicators.note: receiving something takes it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, from joke
over here means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: forty winks is a nap, a short sleep

explanation.surface: Dad hears the punchline and dozes off without a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan describes an expressionless manner, such as delivering a joke unsmiling.

clue.text: Make light of sad performance

parts.note: feeling down means feeling sad
a play is a theatrical performance

explanation.surface: Dismiss a gloomy show as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: To make light of something is to minimise its importance, to understate it.

clue.text: Mountain climbing before meal? They say you reach a level

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
tea is a light afternoon meal

indicators.note: they say signals a word heard, not written

parts.note: the word you is pronounced like the letter U

explanation.surface: Hikers going up the slope before eating learn they will arrive at flat ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high flat land, a level stretch.

clue.text: Castle made of cream and gold, with artificial walls

parts.note: a balm is a soothing cream or ointment
or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A fortress built of dairy cream and gold, enclosed by fake ramparts.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Scotland is a royal residence.

clue.text: Actor Sim is dismissed as a star

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so its letters are removed

parts.note: Alastair Sim was a Scottish film actor

explanation.surface: A well-known actor is fired from his role as a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Field trip made by old women

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, signalling the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Elderly ladies organised an outing to the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often used for hay.

clue.text: Cricketer's second ball gets wicket — England's opener caught in both hands

parts.note: B is second, as in a B grade or second class
O resembles a ball by its shape
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right hands

indicators.note: an opener is a first letter, here of England

explanation.surface: A cricket player's next delivery takes a wicket, with England's top batsman caught by a two-handed catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is the cricketer who delivers the ball to the batsman.

clue.text: British girl's lines and angles?

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name, the possessive just linking
L is short for line, so two lines make Ls

explanation.surface: A British girl's script lines and the camera angles of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevels are sloping edges cut at an angle, so they are angles of a sort, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Spotted dramatic episode, when Oscar's withheld

indicators.note: something dramatic is turned upside down, so the letters are reshuffled
withheld means held back, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Viewers noticed a gripping instalment with the award holder left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from EPISODE leaves EPISDE; 'dramatic' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Espied is an old-fashioned way to say caught sight of, noticed.

clue.text: Yellowish-brown lumps rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: warts are small lumps on the skin

explanation.surface: Pale tan bumps have been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw is a pale yellowish-brown colour, like dried stalks of grain.

clue.text: It gets rid of the reek of corrupt votes — good people are gutted

definitions.text: It gets rid of the reek

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: gutting a word removes its insides, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Something clears the stench of rigged ballots, while honest folk are devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: A stovepipe is a chimney flue carrying smoke and fumes away from a stove.

clue.text: In the news: 9-0 to president

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: N, for new, given twice as the plural news
IX is nine in Roman numerals and O is zero

explanation.surface: A news report of a football score of nine nil for a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th President of the United States.

clue.text: Horse doesn't eat herbs

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
someone who leaves food does not eat it

explanation.surface: A horse refuses to consume the aromatic plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay leaves are aromatic leaves of the laurel used as culinary herbs.
